question: A pre-test loop repeats while the destination has not been reached. What makes it stop?
D: The loop count is always two
explanation: Once the destination is reached, the while condition becomes false.

subject: Programming
question: A process handles one queued item per iteration until the queue is empty. It starts with 6 items and receives no new items. How many iterations are needed?
explanation: Each iteration removes one of the six starting items.

subject: Programming
question: Why must a repeat-until rule specify when its condition is checked?
A: A condition cannot be checked twice
B: All languages use identical loop semantics
D: Checking before or after the body can change the first iteration
explanation: Pre-test and post-test loops can behave differently when the condition starts true.

subject: Programming
question: A loop should stop when remaining <= 0. Why is that safer than remaining == 0 if updates may subtract 2?
A: It forces the value to stay positive
C: It also stops when the value skips below zero
explanation: A decrement of two can pass from one to minus one without equaling zero.
